liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancing In The Street** (2 reviews): The performance is described as a total surprise, following a silky transition from Eyes of the World; The version is particularly great, though noted to be shorter than most other renditions [15][16]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): This is identified as the first instance of the band playing the song in an uptempo style [14]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): The performance of this song is described as very peppy [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-10-01.123211.sbd.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 163 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.gmb.86234.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 156 min; rated 4.42/5 by 12 [3]
- **gd77-10-01.sbd.unknown.277.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: A pop is audible in the recording at approximately the one minute thirty-three mark; Significant audio cuts affect Promised Land and They Love Each Other, with the former suffering sound problems; The recording features a crispy Betty board sound quality [9][11][13]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.ashley-bertha.10689.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 147 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [5]. Said about its sound: The recording has excessive bass, requiring EQ adjustments for most home systems to handle properly; Scratchy distortion is present, possibly caused by Jerry’s refurbished guitar kicking out its newness; The audio is too heavy for a small Sony shelf system, though it should sound incredible on better equipment [18][19]

## Around the show

- Reviewer calls this show essential, comparing it favorably to the October 2, 1977 performance [8]
- This show is seen as a warm-up, lacking the long jams found in the October 2 performance [13]
- The performance is viewed as the start of momentum leading to the October 29, 1977 peak [15]
- The show is considered as good as, or better than, the vaunted Barton Hall performance [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-10-01.123211.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat [1]. Also: Most static in the Estimated Prophet section of the recording has been cleaned up [1]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.gmb.86234.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer..Transferred and mastered by ChrisL.; source: Betty Board (see comments) [3]. Also: Source is a 7-inch two-track BBD reel transferred via PCM501ES and Fostex D5 to DAT [3]
- **gd77-10-01.sbd.unknown.277.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1977-10-01.sbd.cantor.ashley-bertha.10689.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bertha Remaster of the Betty Board source; source: SBD>>MR>>PCM>>DAT>>CDA>>DAW(Bertha)>>CDA [5]. Also: Digitally remastered on April 16, 2002, using a custom dual-DAW setup nicknamed Bertha [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by George Alper Grateful Dead: [1977-10-01 Paramount Theater, Portland, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1977-10-01-paramount-theater-portland-or-usa/) [21]
- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1977-10-01 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1977-10-01-backstage-pass/) [22]
